result.topic_en: A theorem with proof that if a and b are coprime, then ax+by and ay-bx are either both or neither divisible by aa+bb, proved via multiplication of Gaussian-integer identities.
result.transcription:
Lehrsatz
Sind a, b Primzahlen unter sich, so werden entweder beide $ax+by$, $ay-bx$
oder keine durch $aa+bb$ theilbar sein.
Bew. Multiplicirt man die beiden identische Gleichungen
$(a-bi)(x+iy) = ax+by+(ay-bx)i$
$(a+bi)(\alpha-\beta i) = a\alpha+b\beta+(b\alpha-a\beta)i$
in einander, so wird, identisch,
$(aa+bb)\{\alpha x+\beta y+(\alpha y-\beta x)i\} = (a\alpha+b\beta)(ax+by) + ([-a\beta-b\alpha-])(ay-bx)$
$+\{(a\alpha+b\beta)(ay-bx)+(ax+by)(b\alpha-a\beta)\}i$
Bestimmt man also $\alpha$, $\beta$ so, daß $a\alpha+b\beta=1$ so wird
$\left.\begin{array}{l}(aa+bb)(\alpha x+\beta y)\\+(b\alpha-a\beta)(ay-bx)\end{array}\right\} = ax+by$
$\left.\begin{array}{l}(aa+bb)(\alpha y-\beta x)\\-(b\alpha-a\beta)(ax+by)\end{array}\right. = ay-bx$
Die $\left\{\begin{array}{l}\text{erste}\\\text{zweite}\end{array}\right\}$ Gleichung beweiset daß, wenn $\left|\begin{array}{l}ay-bx\\ax+by\end{array}\right|$ durch $aa+bb$ theilbar
ist, auch $\left(\begin{array}{l}ax+by\\ay-bx\end{array}\right)$ es sein werde.

methods.what: Theorem: for coprime a,b, ax+by and ay-bx are simultaneously divisible or not divisible by a^2+b^2
methods.quote:
Sind a, b Primzahlen unter sich, so werden entweder beide $ax+by$, $ay-bx$
oder keine durch $aa+bb$ theilbar sein.

methods.what: Gaussian integer product identities used as starting point
Product identity obtained by multiplying the two identities
Choosing alpha, beta with a alpha + b beta = 1 (Bezout) to express ax+by and ay-bx in terms of each other modulo a^2+b^2
